config.name: How to find a blocked pool
config.markdown: **Start with ALL-pool node counts and CPU headroom; use Selected node pool for exact CPU/memory comparisons and individual nodes.** Negative headroom means assigned application requests exceed usable CPU; positive headroom does not prove a pending pod fits. Application and buffer backlogs are separate below. Buffer target labels use verified current selectors: **POOL = fixed node pool; CLASS = ComputeClass, not one physical pool**. Unassigned application pods cannot truthfully be attributed to a physical pool. GKE desired-node counts are not exposed by the available metrics; requested/available buffer replicas show warm-up delivery, not desired nodes. Missing samples are unknown. Every time-series legend shows **Min · Max · Last**. **History:** capacity v1 records one-minute observations; Min/Max/Last describe the returned chart points, not every raw sample. CPU/memory requests retain the previous regular-plus-init upper bound, not exact scheduler effective requests. Recorded observations expire after two minutes to avoid reviving disappeared nodes at coarse chart steps. Missing recorded history is unknown; this dashboard must be imported only after backfill coverage is verified.
